transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-02
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45m
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Laura Chen (MediCore Head of AI), Dr. Michael Ortiz (Clinical Lead), Samir Patel (Infra), Aisha Gomez (Product)

Summary: Quick kick-off to align on POC goals and draft a quality evaluation plan for clinical summarization / triage assistant.

00:00 Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on this account; with me is Priya our SE. How's everybody doing?
00:08 Laura: Doing well, Jordan, thanks. Excited to get into scope — we've wanted to move faster on a small pilot for clinical note summarization and triage.
00:15 Priya: Great. Today we want to nail down what you consider success, what test data you'll give us, and the evaluation approach — golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination checks, scoring, that kind of thing. We'll also touch security and timelines.
00:28 Dr. Michael: Quick note — accuracy on medication and allergy mentions is non-negotiable. False negatives on allergies are unacceptable.
00:36 Jordan: Noted. We'll make that a hard pass/fail check in the scoring, and then softer metrics for fluency and conciseness.
00:44 Samir: On infra, we need to know whether this can run in our VPC. We're looking at private deployment or dedicated capacity; also KMS for key management.
00:52 Priya: Both supported. For a pilot we usually recommend Redwood Hosted initially to run quick benchmarks, then Dedicated or Private for a production path. We'll document the steps to move to VPC with customer-managed KMS.
01:05 Laura: Ok. For the quality eval plan: we have about 2k triage notes per week. For the POC we'd be able to share ~10k de-identified snippets initially. Does that match your needs?
01:17 Priya: Yes, that's ample. For scoring, we typically ask for a golden set of prompts and expected outputs — annotated examples where you say, this is the correct summary or triage outcome. We'll run candidate models and compute a set of metrics against gold.
01:30 Jordan: Let's talk through the scoring breakdown. From prior POCs we've used: 40% clinical accuracy (entity correctness: meds, allergies, diagnoses), 25% safety/hallucination (false claims), 20% format/structure adherence (templated outputs), 15% latency and token cost. Thoughts?
01:47 Dr. Michael: I'd bump clinical accuracy to 50% and reduce latency weight. Clinical correctness is the priority.
01:54 Samir: Agree on accuracy. For latency, as long as sub-2s for short notes and under 5s for longer ones that's fine.
02:04 Priya: Okay update: 50% clinical, 20% hallucination/safety, 20% format, 10% latency/cost. We'll show per-case pass/fail for critical entities.
02:16 Laura: How do you measure hallucination? We need to know when the model invents a diagnosis or a medication not present in the note.
02:24 Priya: Two parts. Automated checks that compare extracted entities from output to source text (NLP-based string/entity match) and a human review sample where clinical SMEs rate hallucination severity. We'll flag high-risk hallucinations as automatic failures if they concern meds/allergies.
02:39 Jordan: We'll also include a regression test suite — run the current model against previously approved cases to ensure no drop. Do you have existing golden prompts?
02:48 Laura: We have about 150 golden prompts with annotated expected outputs across common triage scenarios. We can export them.
02:55 Priya: Great. For the POC, plan: run 150 gold prompts + 1k random de-id notes + 500 edge-case notes focused on meds/allergies/rare comorbidities. We'll compute Precision/Recall for entity extraction, BLEU/ROUGE for structure, and a hallucination rate metric (percent of outputs with invented entities).
03:16 Dr. Michael: For edge cases, can you ensure the test harness supports PDF and free-text inputs? Some of our notes are OCR'd and messy.
03:25 Priya: Yes, we'll accept the raw text; we recommend pre-processing to remove headers but we can handle noisy text; we'll note OCR error rates separately.
03:33 Jordan: On benchmarks, we'll run both Redwood-hosted baseline models and a quantized dedicated variant to evaluate cost/perf trade-offs. We'll provide a perf table: tokens/sec, tail latency p95/p99, and cost per 1k completions.
03:47 Samir: Do you support KV cache and batching? For throughput testing, that's important.
03:52 Priya: Yep — continuous batching and KV-cache support. In output docs sometimes the term comes out as K V cache or K slash V cache in transcripts, but technically it's key-value cache for autoregressive state. We'll include recommended batch sizes based on sequence length distributions.
04:08 Laura: For golden prompts, do you prefer a single canonical prompt, or multiple templates for different note types?
04:14 Priya: Multiple templates. We'll ask you to label notes by note type (triage, discharge summary, nurse note). For each type we want 10-20 gold prompts covering typical and atypical cases. Also define canonical output schema — e.g., sections SUMMARY, ACTIONS, MEDS_MENTIONED, ALLERGIES.
04:31 Jordan: About hallucination/format checks — format checks will be automated: validate JSON structure against schema, required fields present, value types. Hallucination checks: automated string/entity matching then SME sampling.
04:43 Dr. Michael: For the SME review sample, what's the sample size to be statistically meaningful?
04:47 Priya: We'll propose a stratified sample of 200 cases: 50 gold prompts, 100 random, 50 edge cases. That gives a reasonable signal for human review in a short POC.
04:57 Laura: Scoring thresholds? What's pass/fail for the POC?
05:01 Jordan: Typical gate: clinical accuracy >= 88% on entity correctness, hallucination rate <= 2% for critical entities, format adherence >= 95%, and p95 latency <= 5s. But open to negotiation.
05:13 Dr. Michael: 88% is ok as a starting bar. If we hit 92% we'd look at a production pilot sooner.
05:19 Samir: On security, we need SOC2 reports, network diagrams, SSO/SAML integration, and audit logs. Also support for CME (customer-managed encryption) via KMS.
05:31 Jordan: We'll send SOC2 and architecture docs. Redwood Private supports VPC deployments and HSM/KMS integrations; Dedicated also supports dedicated pools with network isolation.
05:41 Laura: Great. Timeline? We want a 4-week POC starting mid-March. Week1: data handoff and ingestion; Week2: baseline runs and initial metrics; Week3: iterative tuning and regression tests; Week4: SME review and final report. Is that doable?
05:54 Priya: Yes, that's our typical 4-week cadence. We'll need your dataset by 2026-03-09 to hit a mid-March start.
06:02 Jordan: We'll also provide an evaluation harness (script + docker) to run locally in your infra if you prefer. That helps reproducibility.
06:10 Samir: We may run the harness in our VPC. Can Redwood's benchmark agent run inside our environment?
06:15 Priya: Yes — we provide a containerized harness that calls Redwood endpoints, or for Private deployments it can run against the local inference endpoint. We'll send the runbook.
06:24 Laura: Regarding cost metrics, please show tradeoffs: hosted vs dedicated vs private. We'll want clear per-1k completion numbers and an estimate for our weekly 2k note volume.
06:34 Jordan: Will do. We'll include cost per pass at various quantization levels. Keep in mind quantized models may affect accuracy a bit; we'll provide model variants and delta reports.
06:43 Dr. Michael: Any plan for regression tests to catch hallucination regressions after model updates?
06:47 Priya: We'll maintain a regression suite (the golden set + additional failing cases) and run nightly or on deploy. The harness can produce a regression report with flagged deltas. We'll also set up alerts if critical entity accuracy drops beyond a threshold.
06:59 Laura: OK. For evaluation scoring, can you provide a sample rubric? We want both numeric scores and human-readable explanations per failure.
07:07 Jordan: Sample rubric will include itemized scoring per case: entity-level correctness (binary per required entity), hallucination severity (0-3), format pass/fail, latency bucket, and overall composite score. We'll attach example CSV and dashboard screenshots.
07:21 Samir: On integration, what's required for SSO? We use Okta.
07:25 Priya: We support SAML/Okta SSO for the console and audit logs. We'll have you prepare an IdP test connection as part of week1 tasks.
07:34 Aisha: One product question — if the model returns an uncertain answer, can it tag confidence or abstain?
07:39 Priya: Yes, you can request structured outputs with confidence scores and explicit "I don't know" responses. We can tune thresholds and include abstention as a policy.
07:48 Jordan: Alright recap:
- Deliverables: evaluation rubric, prompt set template, benchmark harness/runbook, SOC2 and network docs, pricing estimate, model variants.
- Data: MediCore to send 10k de-id notes + 150 gold prompts by 2026-03-09.
- Timeline: target POC start mid-March, 4-week run.
- Success gates: clinical accuracy >= 88% (preferred 90%+), hallucination critical <=2%, format >=95%, p95 latency <=5s.

08:20 Laura: That matches our expectations. Please include the explicit pass/fail for allergies and meds as automatic fails if missed.
08:27 Priya: Confirmed. We'll add that to the rubric.
08:31 Jordan: Any other questions or concerns?
08:33 Dr. Michael: Just one — how do you handle model updates during a POC so the baseline stays consistent?
08:38 Priya: We freeze model versions for the POC runs. Any tuning experiments are versioned and compared to the frozen baseline; the harness records model hash and container image tags.
08:48 Laura: Perfect. Thanks everyone. We'll wait for your docs and rubric.
08:52 Jordan: Thanks all. We'll follow up with the files and schedule a technical kickoff.
08:57 Samir: Thanks.
09:00 Meeting ends.
